message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to launch a Google Compute Engine instance that has an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and runs Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.  
I’ll give you both the `gcloud` CLI command (the easiest way) and the raw REST‑API payload you could use if you’re calling the Compute Engine API directly.

> **Prerequisites**  
> * You must have a Google Cloud project with billing enabled.  
> * The Compute Engine API must be enabled (`gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com`).  
> * You need a service account key or OAuth token that has the `roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1` role (or equivalent).  
> * GPUs are only available in certain zones – the example uses `us-central1-a`, but you can pick any zone that supports the RTX A6000.  

---

## 1. Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# Variables
PROJECT="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
    --project="$PROJECT" \
    --zone="$ZONE" \
    --machine-type="n1-standard-8" \          # 8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM
    --accelerator="type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1" \
    --image-family="ubuntu-2004-lts" \
    --image-project="ubuntu-os-cloud" \
    --boot-disk-size="100GB" \
    --boot-disk-type="pd-ssd" \
    --maintenance-policy="TERMINATE" \
    --restart-on-failure \
    --scopes="https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform" \
    --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh   # optional: your own init script
```

* `--machine-type="n1-standard-8"` gives you 8 vCPUs and 30 GB RAM – adjust if you need more/less.  
* `--accelerator="type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1"` attaches one RTX A6000.  
* `--image-family="ubuntu-2004-lts"` pulls the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image from the official `ubuntu-os-cloud` project.  
* `--boot-disk-size` and `--boot-disk-type` let you control the boot disk size and performance.  
* `--maintenance-policy="TERMINATE"` ensures the VM is terminated (not stopped) during zone maintenance – typical for GPU workloads.  
* `--restart-on-failure` automatically restarts the VM if it crashes.  

If you prefer a different machine type (e.g., `n1-highmem-16`) or a different zone, just change those flags.

---

## 2. Using the REST API (JSON payload)

If you’re calling the Compute Engine API directly (e.g., from a custom script or Terraform provider), you’ll POST to:

```
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances
```

Replace `{project}` and `{zone}` with your values.  
Here’s a **sample JSON body** you can send:

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000",
      "acceleratorCount": 1
    }
  ],
  "scheduling": {
    "preemptible": false,
    "automaticRestart": true,
    "onHostMaintenance": "TERMINATE"
  },
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": [
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y cuda-toolkit-11-8"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### How to send it

1. **Get an OAuth 2.0 access token** with the scope `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/compute`.  
2. Make an HTTPS POST request with the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header and `Content-Type: application/json`.  
3. The response will contain the operation resource; poll it until `status == DONE`.

---

## 3. Quick sanity check

After creation, you can verify the instance:

```bash
gcloud compute instances describe rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
    --project=my-gcp-project \
    --zone=us-central1-a \
    --format="table(name, status, machineType, guestAccelerators[*].acceleratorType, disks[0].bootDiskSizeGb)"
```

You should see something like:

```
NAME                STATUS  MACHINE_TYPE            GUEST_ACCELERATORS              BOOT_DISK_SIZE_GB
rtx-a6000-ubuntu    RUNNING n1-standard-8          nvidia-tesla-a6000:1           100
```

---

### TL;DR

| Tool | Command / Payload |
|------|-------------------|
| `gcloud` | `gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-ubuntu --machine-type=n1-standard-8 --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud ...` |
| REST API | POST to `/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances` with JSON body shown above |

Pick whichever method fits your workflow. Happy GPU computing!
